core_obligations: Commutators with the raising operators: from the definition of the extended graph the author records that e_i commutes with f_infinity and that h_i acts on f_infinity by multiplication by w_i, for i in I (proof lines 1199-1202).

Spanning the root space by the prescribed shape: the root space of the root minus the sum of the m_i alpha_i minus alpha_infinity is spanned by iterated brackets of the lowering operators f_i with f_infinity, and the displayed identity moves f_infinity across the bracket at the cost of a sign (proof lines 1203-1211).

Highest weight module: the spanning description shows that V is generated from f_infinity by the lowering operators and that f_infinity is annihilated by the raising operators, so V is a highest weight module with highest weight vector f_infinity of weight w (proof lines 1203-1212).

Integrability and the multiplicity statement: integrability is attributed to the cited book of Kac, and then the identification of the root multiplicities with the weight multiplicities of alpha restricted to the Cartan subalgebra h follows from the same source (proof lines 1213-1215).
proof_roadmap: 先用定义直接写出 e_i 与 f_infty 交换、h_i 以 w_i 作用在 f_infty 上。
再把根空间写成 f_i 与 f_infty 的迭代括号的线性张成，用一个交换恒等式把它化成最高权模的形式；可积性引 Kac 的书，重数与权重的对应也引同一处。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the identification of the direct sum of the root spaces of the extended graph with an irreducible integrable highest weight representation and the resulting root-multiplicity formula (author Lemma at source lines 1184-1196, label lem:root). The proof (source lines 1198-1217) does two things: it reads off the commutation relations with the raising operators from the definition of the extended graph, and then shows that the prescribed root space is spanned by iterated brackets of the lowering operators with f_infinity, using a displayed bracket identity that moves f_infinity across the bracket up to a sign (proof lines 1203-1211). That spanning statement is what makes V a highest weight module with highest weight vector f_infinity; integrability and the translation of root multiplicities into weight multiplicities are attributed to two specific sections of Kac's book (proof lines 1213-1215). The step with content is the bracket identity and the spanning conclusion, not the citation. H2.
